subject: Relationship between sigma and relative bias

messages.author: 70d0e9e0688202b7
messages.subject: Relationship between sigma and relative bias
parts:
Hello,

I have a question that arose from the results of simulations of a SECR model of a hair-snare trap grid. The pattern we're seeing is for a given density and a given detection probability the relative bias of the density estimate increases as sigma increases. We were surprised by this and are wondering, what might explain this pattern?

Any thoughts and inputs would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks so much!

Jennifer

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Relationship between sigma and relative bias
parts:
Are you taking care with the mask and/or buffer width? A buffer that is adequate for small sigma may be inadequate for large sigma (resulting in bias). This is why in secrdesign it's usual to specifiy the buffer as a multiple of sigma.
Murray

messages.author: 2c49652a5796ed9c
messages.subject: Re: Relationship between sigma and relative bias
parts: Hopefully this isn't a distraction, but if sigma is large enough relative to the width of the peninsula, you can't observe captures across the full range of the detection function along the minor axis of the peninsula, but you can along the major axis, leading sigma to be underestimated and density to be overestimated.  If the width of the peninsula is say, 6sigma or less (not sure exactly when you'll start seeing bias), you may start to run into problems.  Maybe this is consistent with your simulation results.

parts:
This is certainly relevant, but I'm not convinced. Is this based on evidence? Here's a counterexample (just one replicate, but I'm in a hurry)

library(secr)

grid <- make.grid(20,4, spacing = 20, detector='proximity')
mask <- make.mask(grid, buffer=20, type='traprect')
pop <- sim.popn(D=20, core = grid, buffer = 20, Ndist = 'fixed')

CH10 <- sim.capthist(grid, popn = pop, noccasions = 5, detectpar=list(g0=0.2, sigma = 10))
CH20 <- sim.capthist(grid, popn = pop, noccasions = 5, detectpar=list(g0=0.2, sigma = 20))
CH80 <- sim.capthist(grid, popn = pop, noccasions = 5, detectpar=list(g0=0.2, sigma = 80))

plot(mask)
plot(grid, add=T)
plot(pop, add=T)

predict(secr.fit(CH10, trace = FALSE, bias=NA, mask = mask))

link   estimate SE.estimate        lcl        ucl
D       log 20.4408860  2.79589684 15.6535117 26.6924015
g0    logit  0.2330305  0.03840911  0.1662445  0.3164629
sigma   log 10.1425275  0.69071999  8.8765713 11.5890314

predict(secr.fit(CH20, trace = FALSE, bias=NA, mask = mask))

link   estimate SE.estimate        lcl        ucl
D       log 20.9561244  2.29542039 16.9181478 25.9578741
g0    logit  0.1931234  0.01452266  0.1662411  0.2231891
sigma   log 20.4042143  0.70898921 19.0612744 21.8417696

predict(secr.fit(CH80, trace = FALSE, bias=NA, mask = mask))

link   estimate SE.estimate        lcl        ucl
D       log 20.3174213 2.223092105 16.4062289 25.1610294
g0    logit  0.1940996 0.004867664  0.1847367  0.2038183
sigma   log 80.8163418 1.574675726 77.7885046 83.9620344

My 'peninsula' is about 1 sigma wide in the last example, and the detectors span < 1 sigma in that direction, but there's no indication of bias. (I haven't tried to adjust for the much larger sample size as you increase sigma)
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Relationship between sigma and relative bias
parts:
Thanks for the input so far.

Our simulations were conducted on the university's high performance computing system so the actual code is a little clunky, but here is a clean version that would do the same thing (for a subset of scenarios):

snares <- read.traps("snares.txt", detector="proximity")
mask <- read.mask("ss.txt", header=TRUE)

scen1 <- make.scenarios(D=0.001, sigma = 2000, g0=0.2, noccasions = 5)
scen2 <- make.scenarios(D=0.001, sigma = 5000, g0=0.2, noccasions = 5)
scen3 <- make.scenarios(D=0.001, sigma = 12000, g0=0.2, noccasions = 5)

sim1 <- run.scenarios(100, scen1, trapset=snares, maskset = mask, fit=TRUE)
sim2 <- run.scenarios(100, scen2, trapset=snares, maskset = mask, fit=TRUE)
sim3 <- run.scenarios(100, scen3, trapset=snares, maskset = mask, fit=TRUE)

We used select.stats to extract summary stats from the scenarios.

Here is what we are seeing (for a subset of scenarios):

Look at set of three box plots on the right (g0=0.2). Notice %RB of density is increasing within a given level of g0 (those box plots correspond to the increasing sigmas)

Notice g0 is negative biased at largest sigma (rightmost box plot), which would bias the density estimate high, but why is this happenning?


%RB of sigma not changing with increasing sigma.



To answer other aspects of the discussion. The peninsula is very large: northern Lower Peninsula of the State of Michigan, so I don't think we have an issue with a length-width relative to sigma issue (though some snares are <sigma from the shore. In case it helps, here is an image of the mask (gray dots) and snare locations (black crosses) that we are evaluating with simulations (solid lines included just for boundary references (bear management units):

Finally, we noticed this same pattern in Table 4 (intensive design) of Wilton et. al. (2014). http://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0111257


Thanks again for whatever insights you can provide,
David
